To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reaction degree of the slag and the fly ash in alkali-activated blended systems could be characterized by selective dissolution and NMR spectroscopy.
the increase of the Na2O/SiO2 ratio leads to a reduced reaction degree of the slag with increased Q3(2Al), reduced Q3(1AI) and Q2(1AI) groups.
the increase of the alkali activator modulus leads a reduction of slag reaction degree, and a higher reaction degree of fly ash.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the reaction mechanism, phase composition and reaction products formed in the blended system of alkali activated slags and fly ashes, which is of importance for the application of blended alkali activated binders.
the reaction degree of blended alkali activated slag/fly ash binders, which is of great importance for the development of alkali activated blended systems in the future.

a comprehensive study of the reaction products of alkali activated fly ash and slag, and their blends, which can provide a better understanding of the microstructure evolution of alkali activated binders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

increasing the activator dosage leads to a reduction in the reactivity of both slag and fly ash, while increasing the fly ash content in a blended binder leads to a higher reaction degree of fly ash and a lower reaction degree of slag.
the increase of the alkali modulus reduces the reactivity of slag, and the reaction degree of fly ash is increased, while the reaction degree of slag is decreased.
both the activator modulus and fly ash content influence the phase composition and the reaction degree of the blended binder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the alkali activated slag and fly ash composites can be characterized by 29 Si,27 Al MAS N MR and selective dissolution.

the reaction degree of fly ash is higher than slag in alkali activated fly ash and slag composites, and that the usage of blended binder leads to a reduction in the slag reaction degree with an increase of the fly ash reaction degree.

the increase of activator modulus reduces the slag reactivity; the blended binders show higher contents of newly-formed Q4 groups with lower Si/Al ratio, reduced Q0, shifted mean chain lengths and Si/Al ratios of formed C A S G type gels;
The main takeaway from our work is that
29 Si,27 Al MAS N MR and selective dissolution are useful tools in characterizing the reaction degree of slag, fly ash, and their blends.
the usage of blended binder can significantly increase the reaction degree of fly ash and reduce the reaction degree of slag, which can be used in designing the alkali activation of fly ash.

the usage of blended binder leads to an increased reaction degree and the formation of more polymerized C S H type g gel structures, which can be beneficial for the mechanical and durability properties.
